We run a farm stay business. The Edveros unit we added last season has the highest per-night rate on the property and the highest occupancy. The other accommodation units are traditionally built. The comparison is daily.

We were in a different country on Edveros crane day and watched it live via the app. By lunchtime there was a house on our land. We moved in the following month. That sentence still sounds made up when I say it.
Our Edveros went up on a bank holiday weekend. The crane operator worked the public holiday as part of the pre-agreed schedule. The team took no extra time. The schedule was the schedule.

My GP asked why my blood pressure had come down since a review two years ago. The most significant change in my life since that review: moving into our Edveros. I'm not making a medical claim. I'm noting a correlation.
My neighbour went with a traditional builder the same month we signed with Edveros. We moved in 11 months before him. He still hasn't finished the snagging list.

I wanted to comment on the Tencel in some jeans. I’m the sort of person that has wide swings in clothing sizes. I’m also an endomorph body type regardless of size as opposed to an ectomorph body type—which is probably more of what you are. I took an online body type course by Christie Ressel, and one thing I learned is that certain fabrics can be flattering on some body types more than others. Like for instance with endomorphs, sometimes a more flowing fabric can be more flattering, whereas structured pieces can be more flattering on endomorphs. Think of the structured Levi’s jeans you like—that fabric and style is suitable to your body type, however adding something like Tencel can make a piece more flattering for people with curves at times. I love when I find Tencel in jeans personally, as I find it feels soft and tends to make clothes look more flattering on me. Of course at the end of the day, like with seasonal color analysis, people should wear what makes them happy. But if people are interested in the art and science of how to look good in your body specifically, then I think having rules of thumb for your body type and complexion can be helpful. And that includes different materials at times. My goal when I purchase more clothes to is to prioritize organic fiber pieces that are more flowing and not structured.
